newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast CARB diesel up amid shutdown rumor.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast CARB diesel up amid shutdown rumor.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline and CARB diesel prices led advances early Thursday, lifted by bullish leanings on NYMEX and talk of hydrocracker problems at ARCO's Los Angeles refinery, traders said.
ARCO late Wednesday denied the rumors and declined to comment on why CARB diesel rack prices, normally some of the cheapest in Los Angeles, firmed, according to traders.
Offers for CARB diesel in L.A. rose two cents from late Wednesday to 76 cents a gallon, brokers said.
A slight drop in NYMEX gasoline was offset by an American Petroleum Institute report yesterday that West Coast gasoline supplies fell 1.42 million barrels last week to 26.9 million.
But NYMEX crude kept technical strength in the West Coast spot market, edging up 16 cents to 20.78 at 1112 PST.
Players talked Los Angeles CARB-grade unleaded gasoline firmed 0.50 cents to 76.50/77.50 cents a gallon.
Conventional L.A. grade rose one cent to 73/74 cents a gallon, traders said.
